gloss: gift; treat; refreshments (for workers); care package

definitions.gloss: gift; treat; refreshments (for workers); care package
definitions.explanation: food, drinks, or small gifts brought to people who are working hard, such as coworkers staying late, performers, or students studying

examples.japanese: ファンから{差|さ}し{入|い}れが{届|とど}いた。
{差|さ}し{入|い}れのお{菓子|かし}をみんなで{分|わ}けた。
examples.english: We shared the snacks that were brought for us.

examples.japanese: {残業|ざんぎょう}している{同僚|どうりょう}に{差|さ}し{入|い}れを{持|も}っていった。
examples.english: I brought some treats for my colleagues who were working overtime.

notes:
FORMATION:
{差|さ}す (to insert/give) + {入|い}れる (to put in) → something given/put in (for others)

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
{差|さ}し{入|い}れ is a thoughtful gesture in Japanese culture, showing appreciation and support for people who are working hard. Common occasions include:
- Office overtime work
- School club activities
- Theater/concert backstage
- Moving day helpers
- Hospital visits

COMMON ITEMS:
- お{菓子|かし} (snacks/sweets)
- {飲|の}み{物|もの} (drinks)
- おにぎり (rice balls)
- サンドイッチ (sandwiches)
- コーヒー (coffee)

VERB FORM:
- {差|さ}し{入|い}れる (to bring a gift/treat)
- {差|さ}し{入|い}れをする (to give a {差|さ}し{入|い}れ)

NOTE:
Also has a legal meaning of delivering items to people in custody/prison, but this usage is less common in everyday conversation.

RELATED:
- {手土産|てみやげ} (gift when visiting)
- {陣中見舞|じんちゅうみま}い (care package during busy times)
- お{見舞|みま}い (get-well gift)
